chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim and Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

It was said to him, “By what thing is the Imam recognised?” He said: “By the manifest bequest and by excellence. Indeed, no one is able to cast aspersion against the Imam regarding mouth, nor belly, nor private part, such that it would be said: ‘A liar,’ or ‘He consumes the wealth of the people,’ and whatever resembles this.”

key_terms.أَمْوَالَ النَّاسِ: the property and wealth of other people
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةِ الظَّاهِرَةِ: the clear and manifest bequest or designation
key_terms.بَطْنٍ: consumption or intake, especially regarding unlawful gain
key_terms.فَمٍ: speech or utterance, as a point of possible accusation
key_terms.يَطْعُنَ: to cast aspersion or attack with accusation

ai.seo_question: How is the Imam recognised according to al-Kāfī?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the Imam is recognised through a clear designation and through evident excellence. It also states that the Imam is free from moral and social faults that would expose him to valid accusation in speech, consumption, or chastity, underscoring the purity and integrity required of divine leadership.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, and Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘With which thing is the Imam<sup>asws</sup> recognised (as being the Imam<sup>asws</sup>)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘With the apparent bequest, and with the merit that the Imam<sup>asws</sup> is such that no would be able to taunt upon him<sup>asws</sup> regarding the mouth (something he<sup>asws</sup> had said), nor belly (something he<sup>asws</sup> had consumed and earned), nor private part (for immorality), so it would (not) be said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> is a liar, and he<sup>asws</sup> eats the wealth of the people, and what resembles this’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari who has said the following. “

Once a certain person asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.), “By what thing the Imam is recognized?” He said, “He is recognized through a publicly established will, through excellence in perfection. In the case of Imam no one must be able to raise objections in matters words, of his consumption and sexual matters so that people would say, “He is a liar, usurping other’s properties and such similar things.”
